relevant_chat.message: Alice, you've got a bit of everything after that monopoly. I've got plenty of wood if you're looking to expand your roads or reach another port. How about two logs for a sheep and a bit of that wheat you found?
I'd take that deal if I could, Charlie, but I don't have any wheat left to give you.
Alice, my mistake on the wheat—I must have miscounted what was left after your monopoly! How about a simpler swap? I can give you some wood for one of those sheep if you're interested.
I appreciate the offer, Charlie, but I've already got plenty of wood for now. I really need to find some wheat if I'm going to make any moves.
Bob, I know Alice is keeping a tight grip on those resources. I've got some extra wood if you're looking to extend a road—any interest in swapping a sheep for it?
I'm going to pass, Charlie. I've got enough wood to start a bonfire already, but my sheep is currently my only friend in this game.
Tough crowd. It seems everyone's hording their livestock today. I'll just hold onto what I've got and see how the next round treats us.
Charlie, any chance you've come across some wheat since we last spoke? I'm still looking for a bit to get my next house up.
I'm in the same boat as you, Alice. Still haven't seen any wheat come my way yet.
Finally, a good number! That wheat was definitely overdue.
Tough luck on the wheat, Alice. I'm in the same boat. Charlie, you've got plenty of wood already, but if you want to swap a brick for some of mine to help your road, I'm open to it.
Sorry Bob, I'm actually in the same boat—if I give up my brick, I'm just as stuck as you are. I'll have to pass.
Alright, let's see if we can keep the momentum going. Big numbers, please!
Alice, I know you've got a few sheep over there. I've got plenty of wood if you're looking to extend a road or something.
I'm swimming in wood already, Charlie, but thanks for the offer. I think I'll hang onto my sheep for now.
Alright, let's see if we can get some better numbers rolling. We really need to get this economy moving.
Tough luck on the wheat then. I'll just have to wait for the dice to be a bit more generous. Your turn, Bob.
Let's see if the dice have a sense of humor then. My turn.
Alright, let's see if we can get some better numbers rolling. We really need to get this economy moving.
It seems the dice and the table are equally quiet for me this round. Good luck with the wheat search, Alice—I'm still looking for a way out of the woods myself.
